prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: sideswipe while changing lanes in Houston, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1335; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, but my counsel can confirm it for you.

Q: That's fine. Let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was driving on a surface street in Houston, Texas, heading toward the on-ramp for the interstate. Traffic was moderate.

Q: What were you doing right before the collision?

A: I was in the right lane, and I had my turn signal on because I was getting over to the middle lane to make the exit. I checked my mirror and it looked clear.

Q: What happened next?

A: The other vehicle came up on my left side while I was merging. It sideswiped my car along the rear passenger side. I felt a hard jolt and the steering wheel pulled out of my hands for a moment.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not before it hit me. I only noticed it when I heard the scrape and felt the contact.

Q: After the collision, what did you do?

A: I pulled onto the shoulder. My hand was throbbing, and I couldn't grip anything properly. I stayed in the car until the police arrived.

Q: Let's talk about your injury. What did the doctors find?

A: They said my wrist was fractured. I had X-rays taken at the emergency room, and then I saw an orthopedic specialist a few days later.

Q: What treatment did you receive?

A: They put my wrist in a cast and gave me a splint for the first few weeks. I went to hand therapy twice a week for a while, and I still do exercises at home.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: It's been hard. I'm right-handed, so simple things like opening jars, typing, and cooking took a lot longer. I had to ask family members for help with laundry and grocery shopping for several weeks.

Q: Have you been able to return to work?

A: I went back after a few weeks, but I was limited to lighter tasks. Some days my wrist aches badly by the end of the shift.

Q: Do you have any ongoing symptoms today?

A: Yes. When the weather changes or I grip something for a long time, I feel stiffness and some pain. My doctor says it may improve further, but I'm not back to how I was before.
